doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Gloria Lynne, Milt Hinton and later work
title: Milt Hinton and Louis Armstrong's offer
summary: May recalls playing for Armstrong's band, being told to forget it, and Milt Hinton's versatility.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I’ve heard similar thoughts expressed from Milt Hinton actually.
What a marvelous man he was.

Oh he really was. You know when I was with Billy in the 50s, he was playing with Louis Armstrong, and Billy and I were playing opposite them. And Milt got hung up at a record date. And as a kid, I started, I was playing, maybe I was about fourteen years old. And I shouldn’t have been but I was playing in a trio in a nightclub in the Bronx. And Louis came in and spoke to me and told me how he thought I sounded, and said keep it up and you’re doing fine and all like that. And he knew I was a bass player with Billy’s trio years later. And that particular night when Milt wasn’t there and they were without a bass player he sent word for me and asked me if I would fill in for him. And I was scared to death. And I don’t know whether he got a sense of that or what it was, he said, “Tell him never mind, we’ll just play without the bass.” And it broke my heart. But Milt could play that kind of music, he played in Cab Calloway’s band, he can play straight ahead stuff, and then Dick Katz brought a tape that he made up in Minton’s on that same gig that I was playing with Tony Scott, and it was Dick Katz and Osie Johnson, who was a wonderful drummer. So when I couldn’t make the gig, Milt played the gig. And they recorded, they made a tape of this see. And Milt was playing such modern and such things, it was so hip and everything, that it’s just amazing how he could just go and play any kind of music and just be so solid and positive about everything he did. Just amazing. I’m very proud of that, that Dick Katz let me hear that. Really astounding.
